newsitem.title: USA: American's Chicago hub gears up for possible pilot strike.
newsitem.headline: American's Chicago hub gears up for possible pilot strike.

text.p: O'Hare International Airport officials said Friday they will assist passengers whose travel may be disrupted by a possible strike by some 9,300 American Airlines pilots.

O'Hare, one of four major hubs for the Dallas, Texas-based airline was anticipating a busy weekend with up to 220,000 daily passengers. That would be 25 percent more than the average load for the world's busiest airport.
About one-third of O'Hare's flights are American. American is a subsidiary of AMR Corp.

"The bookings this weekend are very high, we see it as comparable to a Christmas season travel day," said Mary Loney, Commissioner of Chicago's Aviation Department, which manages the city's two airports.
The agency planned on adding staff to provide information and cots for passengers stranded overnight as they do in weather crises.

Loney said American normally provides about 25 percent of O'Hare's operating revenues, or about $330,000, and she expected other airlines to make up most of any lost revenue. American is still obligated to pay half that total.
Loney did not anticipate any adverse impact on paying the airport's outstandng debt.
Loney said O'Hare is better positioned than other American hubs because it serves so many other carriers, including acting as United Airlines key hub. United Airlines is a subsidiary of UAL Corp.
Negotiations between American and its pilots union continued in Washington ahead of a midnight EST strike deadline.
